name: Makaba Flathoof
summary: At Camp Aparaje, Makaba Flathoof has lost his home to the Grimtotem clan. He seeks Horde champions to strike back and keep his family safe.

sections.title: Tragedy at Camp Aparaje
sections.body: Makaba Flathoof grieves for Camp Aparaje, his home in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem clan struck without warning and laid the settlement low. Many tauren seek peace and unity under Cairne Bloodhoof, but the Grimtotem keep spreading discord and violence. Makaba is among the survivors left displaced and grieving.

sections.title: A Plea for Vengeance
sections.body: Makaba Flathoof calls on Horde travelers to strike back, since he cannot retake Camp Aparaje alone. He wants the Grimtotem who overran his home to face fierce retaliation for the slaughter of his kin. His chief concern is Grundig Darkcloud, the warlord responsible. Makaba believes his daughter, Kaya, was lost in the attack.

faq.answer: Makaba Flathoof is a tauren survivor from Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem clan overran his home, and he seeks help from Horde champions.
Makaba came from Camp Aparaje, a small tauren settlement in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem attacked and devastated it.
The Grimtotem clan sacked Camp Aparaje. Grundig Darkcloud was among the figures leading them there.

faq.q: What does Makaba want Horde adventurers to do?
faq.answer: Makaba wants Horde champions to avenge his fallen home by cutting down the Grimtotem at Camp Aparaje and eliminating their leader, Grundig Darkcloud.
Kaya Flathoof is Makaba's daughter. She vanished in the attack on Camp Aparaje, and her family believes she was lost in the assault.

faq.q: Is Makaba related to Dim Flathoof?
faq.answer: Makaba and Dim share the Flathoof surname, but their family relationship is unconfirmed.

angles.text: As a tauren, you see the Grimtotem's bitter treachery in Makaba's plight. Some of your kin honor neither peace nor unity.
As a Horde champion, you can answer Makaba's call for aid and punish those who butcher peaceful encampments.
